en.title: Executive purpose and institutional promise
en.body:
## 1.1 What this dossier is for
An architecture dossier must help leaders decide what the organization is building, which responsibilities it must retain and what evidence would justify investment. A list of technologies cannot answer those questions. ZAF connects purpose, capabilities, operating constraints and engineering decisions in a record that can be challenged and revised.
This public edition is a reference method with a fictional institutional example. It is not a client blueprint, a certification, an implementation claim or a substitute for the institution’s authority. The example is a regional service institution with a headquarters, six offices and an assumed two-person engineering team. Its first scope is operational requests and consolidated reporting; payments, national identity and nationwide deployment are excluded.
## 1.2 The promise to protect
For the selected workflow, an accepted request must have an identifiable origin, an authorized decision, a traceable version and a recoverable outcome. “Accepted” means acknowledged by the authoritative service, not merely stored on a disconnected device. The promise remains meaningful if the technology changes.
A request may be delayed or rejected for a stated reason. It must not silently become two requests after a retry, inherit approval for changed content or vanish between application and reporting. These are candidate invariants for stakeholder approval, not properties already demonstrated by this example.
## 1.3 Executive assessment
The fictional organization can launch separate applications but cannot yet show consistent approval ownership, reporting definitions or a demonstrated restore. The strategic gap is the ability to repeat a trustworthy service across offices. The recommendation is to establish one authoritative journey and common supporting capabilities before multiplying services.
| Executive question | Recommended position | Decision authority |
| What is the first investment? | One approval journey with explainable reporting | Business sponsor |
| What remains institution-owned? | Rules, data definitions, access policy and acceptance evidence | Institutional owners |
| What can a supplier implement? | Agreed components and operational services under explicit contracts | Procurement and system owner |
| What is outside the first release? | Final offline approvals and additional regulated services | Sponsor and risk owner |
## 1.4 Reading the architecture as a city
{{figure:city}}
Domains resemble buildings with different purposes. Shared identity, integration, delivery and observability resemble civic services. Governance defines the rules for using them; the platform team operates agreed common capabilities. This analogy explains responsibility and reuse. It does not mean every capability needs a separate service, database or team.
## 1.5 Required executive record
- A signed purpose statement and explicit exclusions.
- The institutional promise and measurable candidate acceptance scenarios.
- Named business, data, system and risk owners.
- A record of assumptions, unresolved decisions and authorized next work.
## 1.6 Decision gate
Proceed to discovery when the sponsor accepts the first journey and assigns accountable owners. Do not approve a technology procurement solely because the target diagram looks complete. The first management decision is scope and authority; detailed component selection follows evidence.

fr.title: Finalité exécutive et promesse institutionnelle
fr.body:
## 1.1 Objet du dossier
Un dossier d’architecture permet de décider ce que l’organisation construit, quelles responsabilités elle conserve et quelles preuves justifient l’investissement. Un catalogue technologique ne répond pas à ces questions. ZAF relie finalité, capacités, contraintes et décisions dans un document révisable.
Cette édition publique présente une méthode et une institution fictive : un siège, six antennes et une équipe technique supposée de deux personnes. Le premier périmètre couvre les demandes opérationnelles et le reporting. Paiements, identité nationale et déploiement national en sont exclus. Ce document ne reproduit pas un blueprint client et ne revendique aucun résultat déployé.
## 1.2 Promesse à protéger
Une demande acceptée doit avoir une origine identifiable, une décision autorisée, une version traçable et un résultat récupérable. « Acceptée » signifie reconnue par le service faisant autorité, pas seulement sauvegardée sur un appareil déconnecté.
Une demande peut être retardée ou refusée avec un motif. Elle ne doit pas être dupliquée par une reprise, conserver une approbation après modification ou disparaître entre l’application et le rapport. Ces invariants sont à valider et à démontrer.
## 1.3 Évaluation exécutive
L’écart du scénario est la capacité à fournir un service cohérent dans toutes les antennes : responsabilités d’approbation, définitions des rapports et reprise restent à démontrer. La recommandation consiste à stabiliser un parcours et ses capacités communes avant de multiplier les applications.
| Question | Position recommandée | Autorité |
| Premier investissement | Parcours d’approbation et reporting explicable | Sponsor métier |
| Responsabilités conservées | Règles, définitions, accès et preuves d’acceptation | Responsables institutionnels |
| Travail du fournisseur | Composants et exploitation sous contrats explicites | Achats et responsable système |
| Exclusions initiales | Approbations définitives hors connexion et services réglementés supplémentaires | Sponsor et responsable des risques |
## 1.4 La plateforme comme ville
{{figure:city}}
Les domaines sont des bâtiments aux usages différents. Identité, intégration, livraison et observabilité représentent des services communs. La gouvernance fixe les règles ; l’équipe plateforme assure les capacités convenues. Cette analogie ne prescrit ni un microservice ni une équipe par capacité.
## 1.5 Pièces attendues
- Finalité, périmètre et exclusions approuvés.
- Promesse et scénarios d’acceptation.
- Responsables métier, données, système et risques nommés.
- Hypothèses et décisions ouvertes enregistrées.
## 1.6 Point de décision
La découverte commence lorsque le sponsor valide le parcours et attribue les responsabilités. L’achat d’un produit ne doit pas être approuvé sur la seule apparence du schéma cible.

en.title: Institutional context and business capabilities
en.body:
## 2.1 Begin with a decision, not an application inventory
The institution needs to authorize operational work, execute the approved action and explain its reporting. An application is one possible means. The capability model describes what must be possible even when offices, software or suppliers change. It should be stable enough to guide ownership without becoming a permanent organizational chart.
For the worked example, discovery follows one request from submission to departmental review, finance approval, fulfilment and reconciliation. Rejected, withdrawn and amended requests are part of the journey. Describing only the successful path hides the decisions that often create operational risk.
## 2.2 Stakeholders and authority
| Stakeholder | Decision or need | Evidence to collect |
| Requester | Submit the correct version and learn its status | Representative request and failed submission |
| Department reviewer | Confirm purpose and completeness | Delegation rules and rejection reasons |
| Finance owner | Authorize amounts and define the reporting cut-off | Policy, approval sample and reconciled period |
| Operator | Act only on an authorized request | Fulfilment record and exception handling |
| Auditor or reviewer | Explain the sequence without changing it | Authorized access and traceability requirement |
A role name does not establish its legal or organizational authority. Interviews must distinguish policy, delegated authority and actual system permissions. A supplier must not invent a delegation rule because it simplifies the workflow.
## 2.3 Capability and responsibility map
{{figure:capabilities}}
| Capability | Accountable owner | First observable result |
| Request management | Business owner | Versioned request and explicit state |
| Approval control | Delegated approval owner | Authorized decision on a known version |
| Fulfilment | Operations owner | Execution linked to approval |
| Reconciliation | Finance owner | Explained differences and assigned exceptions |
| Platform support | System owner | Repeatable deployment and demonstrated recovery |
## 2.4 Local operating constraints
Connectivity, power, language, device sharing and maintenance access must be investigated at each selected office. “Low bandwidth” is too vague to design against. Capture representative conditions, the longest tolerable interruption and which tasks remain possible during it.
For the scenario, disconnected drafting is proposed while final approvals remain online. This is a continuity policy with a cost: an office may have to wait. The business owner must compare that delay with the consequences of conflicting approvals. Offline finalization is a separate decision requiring conflict resolution and delegation rules.
## 2.5 Deliverables and acceptance
The context chapter produces a stakeholder register, one end-to-end journey, a capability map and a constraint register. Validate them in a joint walkthrough with the people who request, approve, fulfil and reconcile work. Record disagreements as open decisions with an owner and a due point. Acceptance means the map describes the agreed responsibilities; it does not mean a production system has been proven.

fr.title: Contexte institutionnel et capacités métier
fr.body:
## 2.1 Partir de la décision métier
L’institution doit autoriser une opération, exécuter ce qui a été approuvé et expliquer les résultats. La capacité décrit ce qui doit rester possible malgré un changement de logiciel, d’organisation ou de fournisseur.
Le parcours étudié couvre soumission, revue du service, approbation financière, exécution et rapprochement. Refus, retrait et amendement font partie du besoin. Le seul parcours réussi ne suffit pas.
## 2.2 Acteurs et autorité
| Acteur | Besoin | Preuve à collecter |
| Demandeur | Soumettre une version et suivre son état | Demande et soumission en échec |
| Responsable de service | Vérifier motif et complétude | Délégations et motifs de refus |
| Finance | Autoriser et définir la période du rapport | Politique et période rapprochée |
| Opérations | Exécuter une demande autorisée | Preuve d’exécution et exceptions |
| Contrôle | Expliquer la séquence sans la modifier | Droits et traçabilité attendus |
Un intitulé de rôle ne prouve pas son autorité. Distinguer politique, délégation et droits réellement configurés. Le fournisseur ne décide pas des délégations pour simplifier le code.
## 2.3 Capacités et responsabilités
{{figure:capabilities}}
| Capacité | Responsable | Résultat observable |
| Demandes | Métier | Version et état explicites |
| Approbation | Autorité déléguée | Décision sur une version connue |
| Exécution | Opérations | Action liée à l’autorisation |
| Rapprochement | Finance | Écarts expliqués et attribués |
| Support plateforme | Système | Livraison reproductible et reprise démontrée |
## 2.4 Contraintes du terrain
Examiner réseau, alimentation, langues, appareils partagés et accès de maintenance dans les antennes retenues. « Faible débit » ne suffit pas : documenter les conditions et l’interruption tolérable.
Le scénario propose des brouillons hors connexion et des approbations finales en ligne. L’attente est un coût métier à comparer au risque de décisions contradictoires. La finalisation hors connexion exige une politique distincte de délégation et de résolution des conflits.
## 2.5 Livrables et validation
Produire registre des acteurs, parcours complet, carte des capacités et registre des contraintes. Les valider avec demandeurs, approbateurs, opérateurs et finance. Tout désaccord reçoit un responsable et un point de résolution.

en.title: Current-state assessment and evidence register
en.body:
## 3.1 Separate observation, testimony and assumption
A useful current-state chapter explains how a finding was obtained. “Users say reporting is unreliable” is testimony. A sampled report that cannot be reconciled is an observation. An expectation that every branch has the same problem is an assumption. All three can guide discovery, but they have different evidential weight.
The fictional baseline contains spreadsheets, email approvals, a legacy application and manual exports. No investigation of a real institution is implied. Candidate sample sizes and test windows must be agreed according to access, risk and the diversity of journeys rather than presented as a statistically representative audit.
## 3.2 Assess one complete transaction
Select a permitted sample of completed, rejected and changed requests. Reconstruct the submitted content, actor authority, approval version, fulfilment record and reporting inclusion. Note where the chain becomes uncertain. Capture minimal evidence with redaction and an agreed retention rule; copying an entire production database is not a default discovery activity.
| Evidence ID | Scenario observation or unknown | Classification | Next verification |
| EV-01 | Different office reference conventions | Constructed finding | Compare permitted reference samples |
| EV-02 | Approval version not linked to execution | Constructed finding | Trace one amendment through fulfilment |
| EV-03 | Backup success is reported, restore time unknown | Explicit unknown | Perform an authorized isolated restore |
| EV-04 | Branch interruption duration not measured | Explicit unknown | Review incident history and a connectivity sample |
## 3.3 Examine the system as operated
Map authentication, data stores, integrations, scheduled jobs, release procedure, backup locations and support responsibility. Include manual workarounds. A spreadsheet emailed after a failed export is part of the operating system even if it is absent from the software diagram.
Evaluate access with positive and negative tests appropriate to the authorized scope. Review how configuration is changed, who can access secrets and whether a departed user can still act. Do not execute disruptive tests or extract sensitive records without an agreed test boundary.
## 3.4 Baselines before targets
| Dimension | Baseline to establish | Candidate method |
| Workflow time | Time between accepted request and final decision | Timestamp sample with exception reasons |
| Reporting quality | Missing, duplicate and unexplained records | Reconciliation of a known period |
| Recovery | Last recoverable state and restore duration | Isolated restore with record checks |
| Support | Repeated manual interventions and ownership gaps | Incident and release walkthrough |
A baseline describes the sample and its limitations. Do not convert a small demonstration into an institution-wide percentage. The output is a defensible starting point for decisions, not a maturity score designed to make the proposed solution look necessary.
## 3.5 Assessment package
Publish a redacted system inventory, journey trace, evidence register and open-question list to authorized stakeholders. Each finding references evidence or an explicit assumption. The system owner confirms factual accuracy; the architect remains responsible for the interpretation and recommendation. Unresolved disagreements remain visible in the decision record.

fr.title: Évaluation de l’existant et registre des preuves
fr.body:
## 3.1 Distinguer constat, témoignage et hypothèse
Un utilisateur qui juge un rapport peu fiable fournit un témoignage. Un rapport échantillonné impossible à rapprocher constitue un constat. Supposer le même problème partout reste une hypothèse. Le registre conserve cette distinction.
Le scénario repose sur des tableurs, approbations par email, application existante et exports manuels. Il ne décrit pas une investigation réelle. Le choix de l’échantillon et de la fenêtre de test dépend du risque et des accès autorisés.
## 3.2 Reconstituer une opération complète
Pour des demandes autorisées, suivre contenu soumis, autorité, version approuvée, exécution et inclusion dans le rapport. Signaler les ruptures de preuve. Minimiser les copies, masquer les données sensibles et convenir de leur conservation.
| Référence | Élément du scénario | Statut | Vérification suivante |
| EV-01 | Références différentes entre antennes | Constat construit | Comparer un échantillon autorisé |
| EV-02 | Version approuvée sans lien d’exécution | Constat construit | Rejouer un amendement |
| EV-03 | Sauvegarde annoncée, reprise inconnue | Inconnu explicite | Restauration isolée autorisée |
| EV-04 | Durée des coupures non mesurée | Inconnu explicite | Historique et échantillon réseau |
## 3.3 Examiner l’exploitation réelle
Cartographier identité, bases, intégrations, traitements, déploiements, sauvegardes et support. Inclure les contournements manuels : un tableur envoyé après l’échec d’un export fait partie du fonctionnement réel.
Les tests de droits incluent accès permis et interdits dans le périmètre convenu. Examiner configuration, secrets et retrait des accès. Aucun test perturbateur ou extraction sensible ne se déduit d’une simple revue.
## 3.4 Mesurer avant de promettre
| Dimension | Référence initiale | Méthode possible |
| Parcours | Délai entre réception et décision | Horodatages et motifs d’exception |
| Reporting | Enregistrements absents ou dupliqués | Période connue rapprochée |
| Reprise | Dernier état récupérable et durée | Restauration isolée vérifiée |
| Support | Interventions répétées | Revue des incidents et versions |
Un échantillon n’établit pas un résultat institutionnel global. Le dossier doit annoncer ses limites.
## 3.5 Dossier de preuves
Livrer inventaire expurgé, trace du parcours, registre des preuves et questions ouvertes. Chaque constat renvoie à une preuve ou une hypothèse. Le responsable système confirme les faits ; l’architecte assume l’interprétation.

en.title: Gap analysis and risk prioritization
en.body:
## 4.1 A gap is relative to an agreed outcome
A missing tool is not automatically a gap. If the institution cannot establish that execution matches the authorized request, the gap is decision integrity. A workflow engine might help implement a remedy, but naming one does not establish the problem or its priority.
For every gap, connect the current evidence to the institutional promise, describe a plausible failure and identify an accountable risk owner. Distinguish a weakness from a realized incident. “Could allow an unauthorized change” and “has caused unauthorized changes” are different claims.
## 4.2 Prioritize consequences and uncertainty
| Gap | Plausible consequence | Priority in this scenario | Required response |
| G-01: approval version is not authoritative | Fulfilment differs from authorization | P1 | Define version-bound transitions and prove rejection of stale updates |
| G-02: restore has not been demonstrated | Service cannot resume within the agreed window | P1 | Establish objectives and perform a restore exercise |
| G-03: reporting cut-offs differ | Managers compare incompatible totals | P2 | Agree one reporting contract and reconcile a known period |
| G-04: retry semantics are undefined | An ambiguous timeout creates duplicate work | P2 | Define command identity and replay tests |
P1 and P2 are ordering labels for this constructed example. They are not a calibrated institutional risk rating. Actual likelihood, financial impact and legal consequence need local evidence and authorized interpretation.
## 4.3 Follow the dependency chain
Fixing reporting before agreeing the authoritative approval state may encode an unstable definition. Replicating an unrecoverable system to more offices increases exposure. The sequence therefore begins with authority and recovery requirements, then validates one journey, then expands coverage.
A high-risk unknown can justify discovery before implementation. For example, data placement may change the feasible hosting design; branch continuity requirements may change the consistency model. Record the decision blocked by each unknown and what evidence would release it.
## 4.4 Remediation options
For G-01, compare retaining the current application with a controlled versioned approval extension against replacing the workflow completely. The narrower extension may reduce migration risk if the existing system can support the required invariants. Replacement becomes more plausible when ownership, testing or integration constraints make that extension unsafe.
For G-02, a backup product purchase alone is insufficient. The remedy includes protected backup access, a known recovery point, an isolated restoration procedure and a responsible person able to demonstrate it. The institution must accept residual risks such as recovery delay and manual reconciliation.
## 4.5 Risk acceptance and closure
- Record the finding, evidence reference, consequence and owner.
- Compare feasible treatment options and their operating costs.
- Define an observable closure test and the evidence to retain.
- Record residual risk, exception authority and the next review trigger.
A gap is closed when the agreed evidence supports closure, not when a ticket is marked done. The architect recommends treatment; the authorized institutional owner accepts residual risk.

fr.title: Analyse des écarts et priorisation des risques
fr.body:
## 4.1 Un écart se mesure à un résultat convenu
L’absence d’un outil n’est pas automatiquement un écart. Si l’exécution ne peut pas être reliée à l’autorisation, l’écart concerne l’intégrité de la décision. Un moteur de workflow peut contribuer au traitement, sans définir à lui seul le problème.
Distinguer faiblesse et incident : une modification non autorisée possible n’est pas une modification démontrée.
## 4.2 Classer conséquences et inconnues
| Écart | Conséquence possible | Priorité du scénario | Réponse |
| G-01 : version approuvée non autoritative | Exécution différente de l’autorisation | P1 | Transitions liées aux versions et refus des versions périmées |
| G-02 : reprise non démontrée | Service indisponible au-delà du délai accepté | P1 | Objectifs et restauration vérifiée |
| G-03 : périodes de reporting différentes | Totaux incompatibles | P2 | Contrat et rapprochement |
| G-04 : reprises non définies | Travail en double | P2 | Identifiant de commande et tests de répétition |
Ces priorités ordonnent un exemple ; elles ne représentent pas une notation institutionnelle validée.
## 4.3 Respecter les dépendances
Construire le rapport avant de définir l’état faisant autorité peut figer une mauvaise interprétation. Étendre un service non récupérable augmente l’exposition. Commencer par autorité et reprise, vérifier un parcours puis élargir.
Une inconnue peut bloquer la conception : localisation des données, durée des coupures, règles de continuité. Associer chaque inconnue à la décision empêchée et à la preuve attendue.
## 4.4 Comparer les traitements
Pour G-01, comparer une extension contrôlée de l’application existante à un remplacement complet. L’extension limite parfois la migration, si les invariants peuvent être vérifiés. Le remplacement se justifie lorsque propriété, tests ou intégrations empêchent une extension sûre.
Pour G-02, l’achat d’un produit de sauvegarde ne suffit pas. Prévoir accès protégés, état récupérable, procédure isolée et responsable capable de démontrer la reprise.
## 4.5 Acceptation et clôture
- Constat et référence de preuve.
- Options, coûts d’exploitation et recommandation.
- Test de clôture observable.
- Risque résiduel, autorité d’exception et déclencheur de revue.
L’architecte recommande ; le responsable institutionnel autorisé accepte le risque résiduel. Un ticket terminé ne constitue pas la preuve de clôture.

en.title: Architecture principles and quality scenarios
en.body:
## 5.1 Principles must constrain a real decision
“Secure, scalable and modern” does not help resolve a conflict. A principle should state a rule, its rationale, the decisions it changes and the procedure for an exception. It should survive replacement of a framework, database or supplier.
For the example, approval authority, traceable information and recoverable operation take precedence over adding distributed components. That does not prohibit distribution. It requires a reason and the operating capacity to support it.
| Principle | Rationale | Consequence | Exception record |
| Purpose before technology | Capabilities outlive products | Select components against approved requirements | Business need, alternatives and review point |
| One authority per fact | Conflicting copies undermine decisions | Every projection identifies its source and cut-off | Reconciliation and conflict policy |
| Explicit responsibility | Shared infrastructure can hide ownership | Every critical service has an accountable owner | Named temporary delegate and expiry |
| Recoverability by evidence | Backup configuration does not prove restoration | Exercise recovery against agreed objectives | Risk acceptance and remediation owner |
## 5.2 Turn qualities into scenarios
A quality scenario identifies the actor, stimulus, operating condition, expected response and measure. “Fast approval” should distinguish software response from the human approval interval. Improving API latency cannot solve a policy queue awaiting an absent approver.
| Scenario | Candidate response | Verification |
| Two actors approve the same version | At most one permitted transition commits | Concurrent sessions with known initial state |
| Response is lost after acceptance | Same command identifier retrieves the original outcome | Interrupt the client response and retry |
| Worker is unavailable | Committed approval remains valid; work is recoverable | Pause, restart and inspect pending work |
| Service must be restored | Candidate RPO 24 h and RTO 4 h, subject to approval | Timed isolated restore and reconciliation |
The numbers above are design assumptions for the fictional case. They become commitments only after impact analysis, cost discussion and demonstrated feasibility.
## 5.3 Security and continuity can conflict
Requiring online authority preserves consistency but may interrupt a branch during a network failure. Allowing offline approvals may preserve local activity while creating conflicts the institution cannot resolve. Document that tension explicitly. A cache is a technical mechanism; the authority policy is a business decision.
Similarly, keeping all data forever can aid investigation while violating retention requirements. Choose the minimum evidence needed for the approved purpose, with controlled access and an authorized retention rule.
## 5.4 Principle review
The architecture review records where a principle was applied, where it conflicts with another objective and who approves an exception. Review exceptions when their trigger occurs rather than letting temporary workarounds silently become permanent standards.
The chapter is accepted when stakeholders can use the principles to explain a selected option and reject an unsuitable one. If every possible solution “complies,” the principles are not specific enough.

fr.title: Principes d’architecture et scénarios de qualité
fr.body:
## 5.1 Un principe doit orienter une décision réelle
« Sécurisé, scalable et moderne » ne permet pas d’arbitrer. Un principe indique règle, justification, conséquence et procédure d’exception. Il doit survivre au remplacement d’un produit.
Dans l’exemple, autorité, traçabilité et reprise priment sur la multiplication des composants distribués. La distribution reste possible lorsqu’un besoin et une capacité d’exploitation la justifient.
| Principe | Justification | Conséquence |
| Finalité avant technologie | Les capacités durent plus que les produits | Choix fondés sur les exigences |
| Une autorité par fait | Éviter les copies contradictoires | Source et instant de référence identifiés |
| Responsabilité explicite | Le partage peut masquer l’autorité | Un responsable par service critique |
| Reprise démontrée | La configuration ne prouve pas la restauration | Exercice conforme aux objectifs |
## 5.2 Écrire des scénarios vérifiables
Préciser acteur, événement, contexte, réponse et mesure. Séparer délai logiciel et attente d’une décision humaine.
| Scénario | Réponse attendue | Vérification |
| Deux approbations de la même version | Une seule transition permise validée | Sessions concurrentes |
| Réponse perdue après réception | Résultat initial récupérable par la même clé | Interruption et reprise |
| Worker indisponible | Décision conservée et travail récupérable | Arrêt puis redémarrage |
| Restauration nécessaire | RPO candidat 24 h, RTO candidat 4 h | Restauration isolée et rapprochement |
Ces objectifs sont des hypothèses. Ils deviennent des engagements après analyse d’impact, coûts et preuve de faisabilité.
## 5.3 Arbitrer les tensions
L’autorité en ligne préserve la cohérence mais interrompt une antenne pendant une coupure. L’approbation hors connexion maintient l’activité au prix de conflits possibles. Documenter l’arbitrage : le cache ne définit pas l’autorité.
De même, une conservation illimitée peut faciliter l’enquête mais contredire les obligations de suppression. Choisir les preuves nécessaires, leurs accès et leur durée autorisée.
## 5.4 Réviser les exceptions
Chaque exception indique motif, responsable, durée et condition de revue. Un principe est utile lorsqu’il permet d’expliquer un choix et d’écarter une option inadaptée.

en.title: Business domains and shared platform capabilities
en.body:
## 6.1 Separate what changes for different reasons
A business domain owns the meaning and rules of its work. A shared platform capability provides a repeatable service used by several domains. Technology implements either responsibility. Infrastructure hosts the implementation. Keeping those categories distinct prevents the architecture from becoming an inventory organized around product names.
In the fictional institution, request management owns request versions and transitions. Fulfilment owns execution facts. Finance owns reconciliation and reporting definitions. Shared identity establishes authenticated actors; it does not decide whether a particular actor may approve a particular request. That authorization remains connected to the domain policy.
## 6.2 Responsibility boundaries
{{figure:domains}}
| Boundary | Owns | Must not silently own |
| Request domain | Request lifecycle and approved version | Execution evidence created by operations |
| Fulfilment domain | Actions performed and operational exceptions | Changes to a finance approval |
| Finance domain | Reconciliation rules and report definitions | Undocumented correction of source facts |
| Shared platform | Identity integration, delivery, common telemetry | All business decisions |
## 6.3 Share capabilities without creating a bottleneck
Shared does not mean centrally approving every small change. Define a service contract: what the capability provides, who operates it, how consumers gain access and what changes require coordination. A notification capability accepts a delivery intention; it must not become the authority for whether the originating decision was valid.
For a small team, these responsibilities can exist as modules and assigned duties within one deployment. The diagram does not mandate six independent services. Separate deployment requires evidence of a need such as independent ownership, isolation or release cadence, together with a support model.
## 6.4 Federation needs enforceable agreements
Common rules cover identity claims, audit identifiers, contract compatibility and operational handover. Domain owners retain specific policy decisions within those rules. Exceptions require an owner and review trigger. A central architecture function should resolve cross-domain conflicts without taking over every domain’s implementation choices.
When two modules need the same fact, name its authority. A report may retain a projection of an approval, but it must identify the authoritative version and freshness. Directly editing that projection to “fix the number” would bypass the owner and break traceability.
## 6.5 Required artifacts
- Domain boundary map with authoritative facts and owners.
- Shared capability catalog with consumer and support contracts.
- Cross-boundary dependencies and compatibility expectations.
- Rules for ownership disputes, exceptions and decomposition.
The review gate is a walkthrough of an amendment crossing request, fulfilment and finance boundaries. If each owner can explain what changes, what remains stable and how a conflict is resolved, the model is useful enough to guide design.

fr.title: Domaines métier et capacités de plateforme partagées
fr.body:
## 6.1 Séparer les responsabilités
Le domaine métier possède le sens et les règles de son activité. La plateforme partagée fournit une capacité réutilisable. La technologie réalise cette responsabilité ; l’infrastructure l’héberge. Ces catégories ne doivent pas être confondues.
Dans l’exemple, demandes possède les versions, opérations les faits d’exécution et finance les définitions de rapprochement. L’identité authentifie ; elle ne décide pas seule si un acteur peut approuver une demande donnée.
## 6.2 Frontières
{{figure:domains}}
| Domaine | Possède | Ne doit pas absorber |
| Demandes | Cycle et version approuvée | Preuves d’exécution |
| Exécution | Actions et exceptions | Modification d’une autorisation |
| Finance | Rapprochement et définitions | Correction silencieuse des faits sources |
| Plateforme | Identité, livraison et télémétrie communes | Toutes les décisions métier |
## 6.3 Partager sans bloquer
Chaque capacité commune a un contrat : service rendu, exploitant, accès et changements à coordonner. La notification reçoit une intention d’envoi ; elle ne devient pas l’autorité de l’approbation.
Une petite équipe peut réaliser ces frontières par des modules dans un seul déploiement. Le dessin n’impose pas des microservices. Une séparation d’exécution exige un besoin et une capacité de support.
## 6.4 Gouvernance fédérée
Les règles communes couvrent identité, audit, compatibilité et transfert opérationnel. Les domaines conservent leurs politiques. Les exceptions sont attribuées et révisables.
Une projection de reporting doit indiquer sa source et sa fraîcheur. La modifier directement pour corriger un total contournerait le propriétaire du fait.
## 6.5 Validation
Livrer carte des domaines, catalogue partagé, dépendances et procédure d’arbitrage. Rejouer un amendement entre demandes, opérations et finance. Chaque responsable doit expliquer son autorité et ses limites.

en.title: Target architecture and end-to-end behaviour
en.body:
## 7.1 Recommendation and rationale
The proposed first target is a modular application with an authoritative relational store and recoverable background work. This is a scenario-specific response to limited operating capacity and a need for transactional integrity. It is not a statement that a modular application is suitable for every institutional platform.
The target keeps workflow transitions, permission decisions and request versions close to their authoritative data. Reporting and notification delivery are separated logically because they can tolerate delay and have different failure behaviour. That separation can be implemented within a controlled deployment before introducing independently operated services.
## 7.2 Logical architecture
{{figure:target}}
The browser sends an authenticated command with an expected version and stable command identity. The API derives the actor from authenticated context, checks organizational scope and validates the transition. A transaction records the new state, audit entry, command result and any outbox intention.
The worker processes committed background work. A notification failure must not undo an accepted approval. The report projection identifies its source and processing cut-off. Attachment storage, identity provider and backup destination remain separate controlled boundaries even when omitted from a simplified drawing.
## 7.3 Successful journey and rejected journey
| Step | Successful path | Explicit failure response |
| Submit | One accepted request version is recorded | Invalid or incomplete data receives a defined rejection |
| Review | Authorized actor inspects the current version | Wrong department or withdrawn authority is refused |
| Approve | Permitted transition commits atomically | Stale version causes a conflict requiring review |
| Fulfil | Execution references the approved version | Changed or cancelled authority prevents execution |
| Report | Defined source state enters a reconciled projection | Missing coverage is exposed or publication withheld |
Do not conflate a rejected command with a failed service. A forbidden approval may be correct system behaviour. Telemetry and support procedures must distinguish business rejection, technical failure and an outcome the client cannot yet determine.
## 7.4 Concurrency and recovery boundary
A read followed by an unconditional update is not sufficient to protect an approval version. Select a conditional update or locking strategy and test competing sessions. Scope command keys, compare repeated payloads and decide their retention. Transaction isolation is a mechanism to choose deliberately, not a label guaranteeing every invariant.
The architectural acceptance includes a lost response after commit, a concurrent edit before approval and a stopped worker. Each scenario must leave the authoritative state explainable. The exact implementation belongs to the design package and code review; this dossier does not claim that the example has been built.
## 7.5 Target review outputs
Produce a context diagram, logical view, state-transition definition, trust boundaries and failure scenarios. Link each target element to a requirement or gap. If a component has no responsibility, requirement or operational owner, remove it or explain why it is needed.

fr.title: Architecture cible et fonctionnement de bout en bout
fr.body:
## 7.1 Recommandation
La première cible proposée est une application modulaire, une base relationnelle faisant autorité et des traitements différés récupérables. Elle répond à l’équipe supposée et au besoin de cohérence transactionnelle ; ce n’est pas une règle universelle.
Versions, autorisations et transitions restent proches des données de référence. Reporting et notification sont séparés logiquement car leurs délais et défaillances diffèrent.
## 7.2 Vue logique
{{figure:target}}
Le navigateur transmet une commande authentifiée, une version attendue et un identifiant stable. L’API vérifie acteur, périmètre et transition. Une transaction conserve état, audit, résultat et intention de traitement différé.
Le worker traite le travail validé. L’échec d’un email n’annule pas l’approbation. Le rapport indique source et période de traitement. Identité, pièces jointes et sauvegardes constituent aussi des frontières contrôlées.
## 7.3 Parcours normal et refus
| Étape | Résultat normal | Refus ou exception |
| Soumission | Version reçue une seule fois | Données invalides refusées |
| Revue | Acteur autorisé sur version actuelle | Mauvais périmètre refusé |
| Approbation | Transition atomique | Version périmée en conflit |
| Exécution | Référence à l’autorisation | Autorisation annulée ou changée refusée |
| Rapport | Projection rapprochée | Couverture manquante visible |
Un refus métier peut être le bon fonctionnement du système. Il doit être distingué d’une panne technique ou d’un résultat encore inconnu.
## 7.4 Concurrence
Lire puis modifier sans condition ne protège pas la version approuvée. Choisir et tester mise à jour conditionnelle ou verrouillage. Définir périmètre, comparaison et conservation des clés de commande.
L’acceptation couvre réponse perdue après validation, modification concurrente et arrêt du worker. Chaque scénario doit laisser l’état explicable.
## 7.5 Livrables
Fournir contexte, vue logique, transitions, frontières de confiance et scénarios d’échec. Chaque composant doit répondre à une exigence et posséder un responsable.

en.title: Data architecture, ownership and trustworthy reporting
en.body:
## 8.1 Assign authority before designing a warehouse
The institution needs an agreed meaning for request, approval, fulfilment and outstanding obligation. A database schema can encode a definition; it cannot establish its institutional authority. Name the owner who decides the meaning, the steward who investigates exceptions and the technical custodian who operates storage.
For the example, a request version is authoritative in the request domain. Execution facts belong to operations. The finance report combines those facts under an approved contract without rewriting their source meaning.
## 8.2 Information model
| Information object | Authority | Key relationship | Control |
| Request version | Request owner | Stable request ID plus version | Changes do not silently retain approval |
| Approval decision | Delegated authority | References exact request version | Actor, scope and decision time retained |
| Fulfilment entry | Operations owner | References authorization | Partial and reversed execution distinguished |
| Report publication | Finance owner | Contract version and source cut-off | Coverage and revision visible |
| Exception | Assigned steward | Source reference and rule version | Resolution does not erase original evidence |
Retention and access apply to these objects and their copies. The design must identify sensitive fields, attachment handling and any permitted use in test environments. “Keep raw data” is not a blanket permission to retain everything indefinitely.
## 8.3 Source-to-report lineage
{{figure:data}}
Separate business event time, arrival time and publication time. A branch may submit Monday’s execution after reconnecting on Wednesday. Replacing the business timestamp with ingestion time would change the report’s meaning. Record corrections as revisions or authorized adjustments according to the institution’s policy.
## 8.4 Reporting contract and quality controls
Define grain, included states, period, currency treatment, expected sources and late-arrival policy. For one known cut-off, reconcile eligible source records against accepted records and identified exceptions, where those sets are mutually exclusive by definition.
- Missing references remain visible with a responsible steward.
- Repeated input does not duplicate an accepted fact.
- Corrections have a version policy and a replay test.
- Publication states whether expected sources are complete.
- A successful processing job does not by itself establish correct totals.
## 8.5 Analytical evolution and AI readiness
A daily projection is proposed initially because the scenario has not established a real-time decision need. Introduce a separate analytical platform when history, isolation or analytical workload justifies the additional operating contract.
AI use requires a separate problem definition, permitted data use, evaluation set, error consequences and human oversight. A clean data pipeline does not prove a model is appropriate. Begin with traceable data and a measurable decision problem; do not label ordinary reporting as AI to make the architecture appear more advanced.
## 8.6 Acceptance package
The data owner approves definitions and retention. Finance signs off a representative reconciliation. Engineering demonstrates replay and correction behaviour. The architecture record links source objects to report fields and exposes unresolved quality limitations before the report is relied upon.

fr.title: Architecture des données, propriété et reporting fiable
fr.body:
## 8.1 Attribuer l’autorité
Le schéma traduit une définition mais ne lui donne pas son autorité institutionnelle. Nommer propriétaire du sens, responsable des exceptions et exploitant technique.
La version appartient au domaine demandes, l’exécution aux opérations et le contrat de rapport à la finance.
## 8.2 Modèle d’information
| Objet | Autorité | Relation et contrôle |
| Version de demande | Responsable demandes | Identifiant et version stables |
| Approbation | Autorité déléguée | Référence exacte, acteur et périmètre |
| Exécution | Opérations | Autorisation et exécution partielle distinguées |
| Publication | Finance | Contrat, période et révision |
| Exception | Responsable attribué | Source, règle et résolution traçables |
Définir champs sensibles, pièces jointes, copies et données autorisées en test. La conservation des sources n’autorise pas une rétention illimitée.
## 8.3 Traçabilité source-rapport
{{figure:data}}
Distinguer date métier, arrivée et publication. Une opération de lundi transmise mercredi ne doit pas changer de sens parce que sa date d’import est utilisée. Les corrections suivent une politique approuvée.
## 8.4 Contrat et qualité
Définir granularité, états inclus, période, devises, sources attendues et retards. Sur une période connue, rapprocher les enregistrements éligibles des données acceptées et exceptions identifiées, avec des ensembles exclusifs.
- Références absentes visibles et attribuées.
- Reprises sans duplication des faits.
- Corrections versionnées et testées.
- Couverture des sources publiée.
- Succès du traitement distinct de la justesse du résultat.
## 8.5 Évolution analytique et IA
Une projection quotidienne répond au scénario initial. Un entrepôt séparé ou du streaming exige un besoin d’historisation, d’isolation ou de fraîcheur démontré.
L’IA demande un problème défini, des usages permis, un jeu d’évaluation, une analyse des erreurs et une supervision humaine. Une pipeline propre ne prouve pas qu’un modèle convient.
## 8.6 Acceptation
Propriétaire des données : définitions et conservation. Finance : rapprochement. Ingénierie : reprises et corrections. Le dossier expose les limites de qualité avant utilisation.

en.title: Integration, APIs and event contracts
en.body:
## 9.1 Distinguish a command from a fact
A command asks an authority to decide or perform an action. An event describes a fact that has already occurred under a named authority. An API can carry either interaction; a broker does not turn an invalid fact into a valid one.
In the worked example, ApproveRequest is a command directed to the request boundary. RequestApproved is a fact emitted only after a valid transition commits. A notification service may consume the fact but cannot change what was approved.
## 9.2 Contract fields and semantics
| Contract element | Required definition | Failure if omitted |
| Actor and organizational scope | Derived and checked by the authoritative service | A valid account acts in the wrong department |
| Request ID and expected version | Identify the object actually reviewed | Approval silently targets changed content |
| Command identity | Scope, payload comparison and retention | Retry creates another business operation |
| Event identity and schema version | Stable event ID and compatible meaning | Consumers misinterpret or duplicate work |
| Failure response | Rejection, conflict, retryable failure or unknown outcome | Client retries blindly |
## 9.3 Commit and delivery sequence
{{figure:integration}}
Record the state change and outbox intention within one transaction. A worker claims committed work, delivers it and records progress. If delivery succeeds but acknowledgement is lost, processing may repeat. Consumers therefore require deduplication or idempotent effects; the outbox is not an end-to-end exactly-once guarantee.
Ordering should be specified per business object when later facts depend on earlier ones. A global ordering requirement can impose unnecessary coordination. Decide how a consumer detects a missing predecessor, retries processing and exposes work that cannot proceed.
## 9.4 Compatibility and partner onboarding
Changing a field name is not the only breaking change. Reinterpreting “approved amount,” changing currency meaning or omitting an event for a previously included state can break a consumer without changing the schema shape.
Maintain contract owner, version, example payloads, error catalogue and deprecation policy. Before a new integration is enabled, verify identity, permitted data, rate behaviour, timeout handling, replay behaviour and a named support route. Do not treat possession of an API key as agreement on business responsibility.
## 9.5 Verification matrix
- Repeat the same command after an ambiguous timeout.
- Change the payload while reusing its key and verify a defined refusal.
- Deliver an event twice and verify one intended business effect.
- Process a compatible old payload and reject an unsupported version clearly.
- Interrupt the worker and recover pending work without losing its trace.
The output is a contract catalogue and testable interaction design. A broker or gateway purchase follows only when its capability is required and operated.

fr.title: Intégration, API et contrats événementiels
fr.body:
## 9.1 Commande et fait
Une commande demande à une autorité de décider. Un événement décrit un fait validé sous une autorité nommée. Un broker ne rend pas un fait valide.
ApproveRequest vise le domaine demandes. RequestApproved n’est émis qu’après une transition valide. Le service de notification ne peut pas modifier la décision.
## 9.2 Contrat explicite
| Élément | Définition nécessaire |
| Acteur et périmètre | Vérification par le service faisant autorité |
| Demande et version | Objet effectivement examiné |
| Identité de commande | Périmètre, contenu comparé et conservation |
| Événement | Identifiant stable et version de sens |
| Erreur | Refus, conflit, reprise possible ou résultat inconnu |
## 9.3 Validation et livraison
{{figure:integration}}
Enregistrer état et intention d’envoi dans une transaction. Le worker traite le travail validé et conserve sa progression. Une livraison peut réussir alors que son accusé de réception se perd : des répétitions restent possibles. Prévoir dédoublonnage ou effets idempotents.
Définir l’ordre nécessaire par objet métier et le traitement d’un prédécesseur manquant. Une exigence d’ordre global peut créer une coordination inutile.
## 9.4 Compatibilité
Changer le sens d’un montant approuvé peut casser un consommateur même sans changer la structure du message. Documenter propriétaire, version, exemples, erreurs et retrait des anciennes versions.
L’intégration vérifie identité, données permises, limites, délais, reprises et support. Une clé API ne remplace pas un accord de responsabilité.
## 9.5 Vérification
- Répéter une commande après délai dépassé.
- Refuser une même clé avec contenu différent.
- Tolérer la livraison répétée d’un événement.
- Définir le traitement des versions incompatibles.
- Récupérer le travail après arrêt du worker.
Le livrable est un catalogue de contrats vérifiables, avant le choix éventuel d’un gateway ou broker.

en.title: Security, trust boundaries and data sovereignty
en.body:
## 10.1 Security is a responsibility model
Authentication proves a presented identity according to a mechanism. Authorization decides what that actor may do to a particular object in a particular context. Encryption protects selected communication or storage boundaries. None of these mechanisms alone establishes institutional trust.
The example requires explicit boundaries between users, application services, administrators, storage and recovery copies. A locally hosted system can still expose data through logs, telemetry, support exports or backup destinations. Data sovereignty therefore needs an information-flow and responsibility assessment, not only a server-location statement.
## 10.2 Trust and information boundaries
{{figure:trust}}
| Boundary | Control objective | Evidence |
| User to application | Authenticated, scoped and permitted action | Wrong-department and revoked-access tests |
| Application to storage | Least privilege and controlled changes | Service permissions and migration review |
| Administrator to infrastructure | Accountable privileged access | Named access, rotation and change trail |
| System to external service | Approved data disclosure | Contract, field inventory and destination review |
| Backup to recovery environment | Confidential and usable recovery copy | Access controls and authorized restore |
## 10.3 Threat-informed design
For a request approval, consider identity misuse, cross-department action, replay, changed content and unauthorized evidence alteration. Identify the asset, actor, entry point and plausible consequence. Prioritize controls against the agreed scenario rather than claiming coverage of every possible threat.
A detailed threat review must include account recovery, service credentials, administrative access, audit access and incident response. Do not store raw credentials or sensitive personal records in application logs. Redaction, retention and access review belong in the operating design.
## 10.4 Sovereignty and supplier responsibility
The data owner approves classification, permitted locations and uses. Legal or policy authority determines applicable obligations; the architect records the requirement and its design consequence. The supplier provides evidence that the agreed boundaries are implemented and identifies subprocessors or external destinations where relevant.
A claim of “fully local” is not accepted until backups, identity services, email, monitoring, developer access and support paths are examined. Conversely, local hosting is not by itself a security guarantee. Capacity to patch, monitor and recover matters.
## 10.5 Security acceptance
The design package contains a trust-boundary view, access matrix, secrets lifecycle, retention decisions, incident escalation and a test scope. Acceptance requires permitted and forbidden journeys, evidence of access removal and a protected recovery exercise. Unresolved risks have named owners and explicit treatment decisions.

fr.title: Sécurité, frontières de confiance et souveraineté des données
fr.body:
## 10.1 La sécurité est un modèle de responsabilités
L’authentification établit une identité présentée ; l’autorisation décide de son action sur un objet et dans un périmètre. Le chiffrement protège certaines frontières. Aucun mécanisme ne suffit seul à établir la confiance institutionnelle.
Un hébergement local peut divulguer des données par les journaux, exports de support, télémétrie ou sauvegardes. La souveraineté concerne aussi les flux, usages et responsabilités.
## 10.2 Frontières
{{figure:trust}}
| Frontière | Objectif | Preuve |
| Utilisateur et application | Action authentifiée et autorisée | Tests de mauvais périmètre et retrait d’accès |
| Application et stockage | Privilèges limités | Droits techniques et revue des migrations |
| Administration | Intervention attribuable | Accès nominatifs et trace de changement |
| Service externe | Divulgation approuvée | Champs, destination et contrat |
| Sauvegarde | Copie protégée et récupérable | Accès contrôlé et restauration |
## 10.3 Concevoir selon les menaces
Examiner usurpation, action interservice non autorisée, répétition, contenu modifié et altération des preuves. Décrire actif, acteur, entrée et conséquence.
Inclure récupération des comptes, secrets techniques, administration, consultation d’audit et réponse aux incidents. Les journaux ne doivent pas contenir de mots de passe ou données sensibles sans nécessité autorisée.
## 10.4 Souveraineté et fournisseurs
Le propriétaire approuve classification, destinations et usages. L’autorité juridique ou politique définit les obligations applicables. L’architecte traduit ces exigences en choix vérifiables.
Vérifier sauvegardes, identité, email, supervision et support avant de dire « entièrement local ». L’hébergement local n’est pas une garantie de sécurité sans capacité de mise à jour et de reprise.
## 10.5 Acceptation
Fournir vue de confiance, matrice d’accès, cycle des secrets, conservation et escalade. Tester parcours permis et interdits, retrait des accès et récupération protégée. Attribuer tout risque restant.

en.title: Infrastructure, delivery and service continuity
en.body:
## 11.1 Define the operating envelope
Infrastructure selection begins with approved data placement, workload, availability, recovery and support constraints. For the fictional institution, local control is a candidate requirement to validate, not a claim about an existing installation. A deployment diagram must distinguish logical roles from independent physical failure domains.
Two containers on one host do not provide host resilience. Replication is not a backup. An untested disaster-recovery diagram is an intention, not a demonstrated capability. Each claim requires a failure model and an exercise.
## 11.2 Candidate deployment view
{{figure:deployment}}
This conceptual view separates access, application processing, authoritative storage and protected recovery copies. It deliberately does not prescribe a highly available cluster for a team that has not established its operating capacity. The final design must choose host count, power, network, storage and recovery locations against approved objectives.
## 11.3 Recovery objectives and cost
| Item | Scenario candidate | Decision or evidence needed |
| Recovery point | At most 24 hours of data loss | Business impact and permitted loss window |
| Recovery time | Restore essential journey within 4 hours | Timed exercise including application and data checks |
| Backup protection | Separate access from routine application operation | Credential and deletion-control review |
| Restore scope | Data, attachments, configuration and keys | Complete dependency inventory |
| Degraded operation | Draft work preserved; final approval waits | Branch continuity and communication policy |
A candidate objective becomes a commitment only when scope, exclusions, dependencies, staffing and cost are approved. Record which functions return first and which manual reconciliation is required after restoration.
## 11.4 Release engineering
Every release identifies source revision, artifact, configuration, schema change and verification result. Required checks follow the risk. A schema change may require compatibility tests and a staged migration; an access change needs negative authorization tests.
The recovery plan distinguishes application rollback, forward repair and data restoration. Reusing a previous container image does not undo a destructive data change. The release owner must know which strategy is permitted before deployment.
## 11.5 Continuity exercise
Simulate a defined failure in an authorized isolated environment. Record detection, decision, restoration, reconciliation and return to service. Compare actual results with the approved objectives and record corrective work. An exercise that omits attachments or required keys cannot establish complete recovery.
## 11.6 Acceptance package
Deliver the deployment view, failure-domain inventory, release procedure, protected backup policy and restore runbook. The system owner accepts operating responsibility; the sponsor accepts the residual continuity cost and risk. Infrastructure complexity expands only when its benefit and ownership are explicit.

fr.title: Infrastructure, livraison et continuité du service
fr.body:
## 11.1 Définir les contraintes d’exploitation
Choisir l’infrastructure après localisation autorisée, charge, disponibilité, reprise et support. Le contrôle local est ici une exigence candidate à valider.
Deux conteneurs sur un même hôte ne protègent pas d’une panne de cet hôte. Une réplication n’est pas une sauvegarde. Chaque promesse demande un modèle de défaillance et un exercice.
## 11.2 Vue de déploiement candidate
{{figure:deployment}}
La vue distingue accès, traitement, données de référence et copies de reprise protégées. Elle n’impose pas un cluster haute disponibilité sans équipe capable de l’exploiter. Hôtes, alimentation, réseau et stockage seront dimensionnés selon les objectifs approuvés.
## 11.3 Reprise et coût
| Élément | Hypothèse | Décision attendue |
| RPO | Perte maximale candidate de 24 h | Impact et perte tolérable |
| RTO | Parcours essentiel rétabli en 4 h | Exercice chronométré et vérifié |
| Protection | Accès distinct de l’application | Droits et contrôle de suppression |
| Périmètre | Données, pièces, configuration et clés | Inventaire complet |
| Mode dégradé | Brouillons conservés, approbation en attente | Politique et communication |
Un objectif devient un engagement lorsque périmètre, dépendances, personnel et coûts sont approuvés.
## 11.4 Livraison
Relier révision, artefact, configuration, migration et vérifications. Tester compatibilité et droits selon le risque. Distinguer retour applicatif, correction en avant et restauration des données.
## 11.5 Exercice et acceptation
Simuler une panne dans un environnement isolé autorisé. Mesurer détection, décision, restauration, rapprochement et reprise. Une vérification sans pièces jointes ou clés nécessaires ne prouve pas la récupération complète.
Livrer déploiement, inventaire des défaillances, procédure de version, politique de sauvegarde et runbook. Nommer les responsables et accepter le risque résiduel.

en.title: Governance, platform ownership and operating model
en.body:
## 12.1 Architecture needs a decision system
A diagram cannot assign authority by itself. Governance identifies who decides, who supplies evidence, who operates the outcome and who may approve an exception. The operating model must fit the institution’s people rather than reproducing the structure of a much larger technology company.
In the fictional two-engineer team, several roles may be held by the same person. The responsibilities must still be distinguishable, and critical approvals need an appropriate independent check. A separate platform capability does not automatically require a separate department.
## 12.2 Responsibility matrix
| Decision or activity | Accountable | Responsible for delivery | Consulted |
| Business transition policy | Business owner | Domain engineering owner | Finance and control |
| Data definition and retention | Data owner | Data steward and custodian | Legal or policy authority |
| Release readiness | System owner | Delivery engineer | Domain and support owners |
| Architecture exception | Authorized architecture or risk owner | Proposing team | Affected consumers |
| Incident coordination | System owner | Named incident lead | Business and security owners |
| Residual-risk acceptance | Authorized institutional owner | Risk coordinator documents | Architect and operators |
Accountability is not transferred to a software vendor by leaving a cell blank. The service contract should explain which responsibilities are delegated and which the institution retains.
## 12.3 Architecture decision lifecycle
{{figure:governance}}
A decision record includes context, evidence, constraints, options, recommendation, consequences and a review trigger. Proposed, accepted, superseded and withdrawn states should be explicit. Retain the rationale when replacing a decision so future teams understand why the earlier choice was reasonable.
A lightweight review may be enough for a local module change. A cross-domain contract or sensitive data destination requires broader review. Classify changes by consequence rather than demanding the same committee for every commit.
## 12.4 Run the service after handover
Define service hours, support route, escalation, access review, patching, backup exercises and exception ownership. Incident response must include business communication and reconciliation of uncertain outcomes, not only restarting the process.
Record operational knowledge where the team can use it. A runbook should name prerequisites, permissions, actions, verification and escalation. Test it with someone other than its author where possible. Personal availability is not a durable support model.
## 12.5 Governance outputs
- Role and decision-rights register.
- Service catalog with operating and consumer contracts.
- Architecture records and time-bounded exceptions.
- Incident, release and recovery responsibilities.
- Periodic evidence review and improvement backlog.
The acceptance gate is a scenario walkthrough: a failed release, uncertain approval or overdue reporting job must have a decision-maker and a response. Governance is effective when that route works, not when the organizational diagram looks complete.

fr.title: Gouvernance, responsabilité plateforme et exploitation
fr.body:
## 12.1 Organiser les décisions
La gouvernance nomme qui décide, fournit les preuves, exploite et accepte une exception. Elle doit correspondre aux personnes disponibles.
Dans l’équipe fictive de deux ingénieurs, plusieurs rôles peuvent être réunis. Les responsabilités restent distinctes et les décisions critiques nécessitent un contrôle adapté. Une capacité plateforme n’impose pas un département séparé.
## 12.2 Responsabilités
| Activité | Autorité accountable | Réalisation | Consultation |
| Politique métier | Propriétaire métier | Responsable domaine | Finance et contrôle |
| Définition et conservation | Propriétaire des données | Steward et exploitant | Autorité juridique ou politique |
| Livraison | Responsable système | Ingénieur livraison | Métier et support |
| Exception d’architecture | Autorité habilitée | Équipe proposante | Consommateurs affectés |
| Incident | Responsable système | Coordinateur nommé | Métier et sécurité |
| Risque résiduel | Autorité institutionnelle | Coordinateur des risques | Architecte et exploitants |
Une cellule vide ne transfère pas la responsabilité au fournisseur. Le contrat précise délégations et responsabilités conservées.
## 12.3 Cycle de décision
{{figure:governance}}
Un enregistrement conserve contexte, preuves, options, recommandation, conséquences et déclencheur de revue. Distinguer proposé, accepté, remplacé et retiré.
Une modification locale peut recevoir une revue légère ; un contrat interdomaines ou une destination sensible demande une autorité plus large. Adapter la revue aux conséquences.
## 12.4 Exploiter après transfert
Définir horaires, support, escalade, accès, correctifs et exercices de reprise. La réponse à l’incident comprend communication et rapprochement des résultats incertains.
Le runbook précise prérequis, droits, actions, vérifications et escalade. Le tester avec une autre personne si possible.
## 12.5 Validation
Livrer droits de décision, contrats de service, exceptions temporaires et responsabilités opérationnelles. Un incident simulé doit trouver un décideur et une réponse, pas seulement un organigramme.

en.title: Technology mapping, economics and decision records
en.body:
## 13.1 Choose an implementation for a capability
Technology is evaluated after the required capability and operating contract are known. Compare options against functional fit, team competence, security, data placement, lifecycle, recovery, integration and exit cost. A familiar product can be a reasonable choice; familiarity alone does not establish its suitability.
For the scenario, the recommendation is a modular backend, PostgreSQL and a recoverable background worker. Specific language and hosting remain subject to maintainers, approved placement and test evidence. Kafka, Kubernetes and a separate warehouse are not initial requirements simply because the long-term vision is ambitious.
## 13.2 Technology mapping
| Capability | Candidate | Why it may fit | Operating obligation |
| Transactional state | PostgreSQL | Constraints, transactions and established relational model | Concurrency tests, patching and restore |
| Workflow implementation | Modular backend | Keeps one approval boundary understandable | Domain tests and migration ownership |
| Background processing | Outbox and small worker | Recoverable deferred effects | Retry, deduplication and stuck-work response |
| Packaging | Versioned containers | Reproducible artifact boundary | Image provenance, configuration and patching |
| Reporting | Versioned projections | Traceable initial daily reporting | Reconciliation, revision and source coverage |
## 13.3 Decision records
| Record | Recommendation | Alternative | Accepted consequence | Review trigger |
| ADR-001 | Modular application first | Independent microservices | Shared release lifecycle | Independent teams or measured isolation need |
| ADR-002 | Deferred notification | Send within approval transaction | Delivery delay and worker operation | Stricter demonstrated delivery requirement |
| ADR-003 | Draft offline, approve online | Final offline approval | Waiting during network outage | Approved conflict and delegation policy |
| ADR-004 | Daily projection first | Streaming analytical platform | One reporting-cycle delay | A decision needs fresher data and operating capacity exists |
These are reference recommendations, not accepted decisions by a real institution. An actual decision record names its approver, date, evidence and conditions.
## 13.4 Evaluate total operating cost
Compare discovery, implementation, migration, licenses where applicable, hosting, connectivity, staffing, support, recovery exercises and eventual exit. A free license does not make operation free. A managed service may reduce some work while adding cost, dependency and data-placement questions.
Do not publish invented savings or precise infrastructure prices for an unmeasured scenario. Build cost ranges with explicit assumptions and sensitivity to workload, retention and service hours. Separate one-time change cost from recurring service cost and the institution’s retained responsibilities.
## 13.5 Exit and replaceability
Name the data export format, contract ownership, recovery materials and knowledge required to change a supplier or component. Technology replaceability is not instantaneous substitution. It is the ability to explain dependencies, test a transition and preserve authority and records during it.
The review gate accepts a reasoned option comparison and its consequences. Product installation is a later delivery activity.

fr.title: Choix technologiques, économie et décisions
fr.body:
## 13.1 Choisir après la capacité
Comparer adéquation, compétences, sécurité, localisation, cycle de vie, reprise, intégration et coût de sortie. La familiarité aide sans prouver l’adéquation.
Le scénario retient un backend modulaire, PostgreSQL et un worker récupérable. Langage et hébergement restent à valider. Kafka, Kubernetes et entrepôt séparé ne découlent pas automatiquement de l’ambition.
## 13.2 Correspondance
| Capacité | Option | Obligation |
| État transactionnel | PostgreSQL | Concurrence, mises à jour et reprise |
| Workflow | Backend modulaire | Tests métier et migrations |
| Travail différé | Outbox et worker | Reprises, doublons et blocages |
| Packaging | Conteneurs versionnés | Provenance et configuration |
| Reporting | Projections versionnées | Rapprochement et couverture |
## 13.3 Décisions documentées
| Décision | Recommandation | Coût accepté | Révision |
| ADR-001 | Application modulaire | Livraison commune | Équipes distinctes ou isolation mesurée |
| ADR-002 | Notifications différées | Délai et worker | Besoin de livraison plus strict |
| ADR-003 | Approbation en ligne | Attente pendant coupure | Politique de conflits approuvée |
| ADR-004 | Rapport quotidien | Retard d’un cycle | Décision demandant plus de fraîcheur |
Ce sont des recommandations illustratives. Une décision réelle nomme approbateur, date et preuves.
## 13.4 Coût total
Inclure découverte, réalisation, migration, licences éventuelles, hébergement, réseau, équipe, support, reprise et sortie. Une licence gratuite ne rend pas l’exploitation gratuite.
Construire des fourchettes sous hypothèses explicites. Séparer changement initial et coût récurrent. Aucune économie ni tarification précise n’est inventée.
## 13.5 Réversibilité
Identifier formats d’export, propriété des contrats, éléments de reprise et connaissances nécessaires au changement de fournisseur. La remplaçabilité est une transition explicable et testable, pas une substitution instantanée.

en.title: Transition roadmap, verification and acceptance
en.body:
## 14.1 Move through evidence gates
A roadmap is a dependency and risk sequence, not a calendar decorated with milestones. The institution should know what must be learned or demonstrated before the next investment. Durations and budgets are agreed after scope and access are known.
The proposed sequence begins with discovery, designs one authoritative journey, pilots it at one office, exercises recovery and expands only after the operating contract works. It preserves an explicit fallback during migration and does not treat data import as proof that business meaning survived.
## 14.2 Phased delivery
{{figure:roadmap}}
| Phase | Deliverable | Exit evidence | Accountable owner |
| Discover | Current map, evidence and approved definitions | Owners resolve authority and reporting rules | Business sponsor |
| Design | Boundaries, model, contracts and threat review | Normal, rejected and interrupted journeys explained | Architecture owner |
| Pilot | One office and one request type | Permission, concurrency, retry and reconciliation checks | System owner |
| Recover | Protected backup and restoration exercise | Approved recovery objectives demonstrated | System owner |
| Expand | Controlled rollout and handover | Support, coverage and freshness demonstrated | Business and system owners |
## 14.3 Migration and coexistence
Identify which source remains authoritative at every stage. Avoid a transition where two applications can approve the same request independently without a reconciliation rule. Plan reference mapping, data quality treatment, cut-over verification and a controlled way to pause or reverse expansion.
Historical records may be incomplete. Record their provenance and limitations rather than manufacturing missing approvals. Decide how legacy evidence remains accessible and who may correct it.
## 14.4 Acceptance scenarios
| Scenario | Required observation |
| Lost response after commit | Retry retrieves the original result without new work |
| Stale approval | Changed content requires renewed review |
| Wrong organizational scope | Action is refused and evidence is retained appropriately |
| Worker interruption | Committed decision survives; deferred work resumes |
| Repeated input | Reporting total is not doubled |
| Late correction | Defined revision policy is applied and explainable |
| Restore | Known records, attachments and dependencies reconcile |
Acceptance tests require a known initial state and expected result. Keep records of version, environment, scope and observed behaviour. A demonstration on a laptop does not establish production capacity or institutional compliance.
## 14.5 Handover and closure
Handover includes operating responsibilities, access, runbooks, support expectations, unresolved risks and the next review trigger. The institution accepts the outcome against agreed evidence; completion does not erase open limitations.
A delivery phase may be stopped if its assumptions fail. ZAF should make that decision legible before sunk cost turns a weak design into an irreversible commitment.

fr.title: Trajectoire de transition, vérification et acceptation
fr.body:
## 14.1 Avancer par preuves
La feuille de route ordonne dépendances et risques. Les durées et budgets seront convenus après définition des accès et du périmètre.
Découvrir, concevoir un parcours, piloter dans une antenne, démontrer la reprise puis étendre. Un import réussi ne prouve pas la conservation du sens métier.
## 14.2 Phases
{{figure:roadmap}}
| Phase | Livrable | Preuve de sortie | Autorité |
| Découverte | Carte, preuves et définitions | Autorité et reporting validés | Sponsor |
| Conception | Frontières, modèle et contrats | Parcours normal et interrompu expliqués | Architecture |
| Pilote | Une antenne et une demande | Droits, concurrence et rapprochement | Système |
| Reprise | Sauvegarde et restauration | Objectifs démontrés | Système |
| Extension | Déploiement et transfert | Support et couverture démontrés | Métier et système |
## 14.3 Migration
Nommer la source faisant autorité à chaque étape. Ne pas permettre deux approbations indépendantes sans règle de rapprochement. Prévoir correspondance des références, anomalies, bascule et arrêt contrôlé.
Une archive incomplète garde sa provenance et ses limites. Ne pas fabriquer des approbations absentes pour compléter l’historique.
## 14.4 Acceptation
| Scénario | Résultat attendu |
| Réponse perdue | Même résultat sans nouveau travail |
| Version périmée | Nouvelle revue nécessaire |
| Mauvais périmètre | Refus approprié |
| Worker arrêté | Décision conservée et reprise |
| Source répétée | Total non doublé |
| Correction tardive | Révision expliquée |
| Restauration | Données et dépendances rapprochées |
Conserver état initial, version, environnement et résultat. Une démonstration locale ne prouve ni capacité de production ni conformité institutionnelle.
## 14.5 Transfert
Documenter responsabilités, accès, procédures, support, limites et prochaine revue. L’acceptation dépend des preuves convenues. Une phase peut être arrêtée lorsque ses hypothèses échouent.

en.title: Future evolution and executive decision package
en.body:
## 15.1 Preserve principles, revise implementations
Long-lived architecture does not predict a fixed technology stack decades ahead. It preserves purpose, authority, data meaning and decision history while making implementation choices revisable. An evolutionary trigger should identify the evidence that makes the present option inadequate.
The initial modular target may remain appropriate for a long time. It may also need decomposition when ownership or isolation changes. Both outcomes are compatible with ZAF if the decision follows evidence.
## 15.2 Evolution triggers
| Trigger | Evidence | Candidate response | New responsibility |
| Independent domain delivery is blocked | Repeated measured coordination cost | Separate a stable boundary | Consumer compatibility and independent operations |
| Reporting affects transactional workload | Representative contention and workload analysis | Isolate analytical processing | Data movement, freshness and reconciliation |
| Branch continuity needs exceed online approval policy | Business impact and approved delegation rules | Controlled offline decision design | Conflict resolution and recovery of local state |
| Recovery target cannot be met | Timed exercise and cost comparison | Change backup or deployment design | New failure domains and operating duties |
| AI use has a defined institutional benefit | Permitted data, evaluation and error analysis | Bounded pilot with human oversight | Model monitoring and accountability |
No trigger automatically dictates a specific product. Re-evaluate simpler changes and the cost of added operating responsibility.
## 15.3 Executive decision package
The sponsor receives a concise decision brief linked to the full documentation. It states the institutional promise, observed gaps, recommended target, alternatives, costs to estimate, unresolved authority questions and the evidence needed for the next gate.
For this example, management must decide data placement and retention, the approval delegation policy, acceptable network interruption, recovery objectives and the staff able to operate the service. Those decisions cannot be delegated to a diagram.
## 15.4 Required architecture artifacts
| Artifact | Purpose | Review owner |
